text: This man just sprayed glass cleaner into a toilet full of bleach, and a cloud is rising.
Up close, the two cleaners start fighting.
Bleach and the ammonia in glass cleaner make a gas called chloramine.
He breathes it in, and it hits the wet lining of his throat and lungs.
There, it breaks apart into acid. His eyes burn, and he can't stop coughing.
Movies say: if the smell goes away, the danger's gone.
Wrong. Ammonia wears out your nose, so you stop smelling it while you keep breathing it in.
Worse: fluid can fill his lungs hours later, up to a full day after.
So he gets out to fresh air, calls poison control, and never mixes cleaners again.
And that's what really happens when you mix bleach and ammonia.
